key_insight: This paper shows that coding harnesses are not all equal: individual design choices like planning, action space, and context management can materially change how well autonomous coding agents perform. By isolating these components, the authors make it possible to see which harness parts actually help long-horizon software engineering.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the lack of component-level understanding in coding agent harnesses. Prior work often evaluates harnesses as a single black box, making it hard to know which design choices drive performance gains or losses.
method: Built a lightweight coding harness with a fixed execution loop to control for confounding factors.
Varied three harness components independently: planning, action space, and context management.
Evaluated the harness across four models to compare component-level effects on coding-agent performance.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this provides a clearer way to design, tune, and benchmark coding agents. It helps teams focus on the harness components that truly improve real-world software engineering outcomes.
visual_elements: A block diagram of the harness loop with highlighted interchangeable components.
A comparison chart showing performance across planning, action space, and context management settings.
A matrix table mapping models to harness variants.
Icons representing code, memory/context, planning, and execution.
paper_title: An Empirical Study of Harness Design for Coding Agents
paper_authors: Run-Ze Fan, Zihao Zhang, Simin Ma, Yebowen Hu, Shouju Wang
